entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Did you know that the Anrakan Fede..."
entries.dialogueText: "Did you know that the Anrakan Federation is building islands in the middle of the ocean?"

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""You shouldn't have. You don't live..."
entries.dialogueText: "You shouldn't have. You don't live in Sordland anymore."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""I thought you would be happy to se..."
entries.dialogueText: "I thought you would be happy to see an old friend."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Ewald's upper lip curled, but he qu..."
entries.dialogueText: Ewald's upper lip curled, but he quickly turned it into a smile.

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""I thought you couldn't sink any de..."
entries.dialogueText: "I thought you couldn't sink any deeper when you handed the Anrakans the keys to our energy. But moving there was an all-time low, even for you."

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""Don't make me laugh, Ewald. You tr..."
entries.dialogueText: "Don't make me laugh, Ewald. You traded Sordland for damn Anraka."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Honestly, I feel the same way. Thi..."
entries.dialogueText: "Honestly, I feel the same way. This was not what I had in mind when I removed the Energy Protection Act."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Yes, Mr. Alphonso. Why did you dec..."
entries.dialogueText: "Yes, Mr. Alphonso. Why did you decide to move to the Federation of Anrakan Isles?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""A former Sordish president who cho..."
entries.dialogueText: "A former Sordish president who chose to retire on an island. Sounds familiar."

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""I chose to remain in Sordland, Mr...."
entries.dialogueText: "I chose to remain in Sordland, Mr. Rayne. My homeland. Not to sell myself off to the highest bidder."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Gentlemen, please. Neither of you..."
entries.dialogueText: "Gentlemen, please. Neither of you can judge me."

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""To live as a king, off of the back..."
entries.dialogueText: "To live as a king, off of the backs of hard-working Sords."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Mr. Soll, please. You are not in a..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. Soll, please. You are not in a position to judge me."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Mr. President, the state's investm..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. President, the state's investment in Gasom helped the company get back on its feet. I'll always appreciate that."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""But after you removed the EPA, the..."
entries.dialogueText: "But after you removed the EPA, the Anrakans made me the deal of a lifetime. I couldn't exactly refuse."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Let me guess. You live on one of t..."
entries.dialogueText: "Let me guess. You live on one of them."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""That sounds impressive. Tell me mo..."
entries.dialogueText: "That sounds impressive. Tell me more."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Is that why you sold Gasom to them..."
entries.dialogueText: "Is that why you sold Gasom to them and abandoned Sordland for Anraka?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Why are you even here, Mr. Alphons..."
entries.dialogueText: "Why are you even here, Mr. Alphonso? You're not invested in the future of Sordland, so I can't imagine you're invested in Sordish football."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Mr. Rayne, please. You are not in..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. Rayne, please. You are not in a position to judge me."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Your hefty investment in Gasom hel..."
entries.dialogueText: "Your hefty investment in Gasom helped the company get back on its feet. I'll always appreciate that."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""But after you removed the Energy P..."
entries.dialogueText: "But after you removed the Energy Protection Act, the Anrakans made me the deal of a lifetime. I couldn't exactly refuse."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""I'm getting old. Surely I've earne..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm getting old. Surely I've earned the right to a comfortable retirement."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I'd rather not discuss this any fu..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'd rather not discuss this any further, Mr. Alphonso."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""You persuaded the Sordish state to..."
entries.dialogueText: "You persuaded the Sordish state to invest in Gasom as a leap of faith -- and then you turned around and sold your own shares."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Don't try to blame me for your own..."
entries.dialogueText: "Don't try to blame me for your own selfishness."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Mr. Soll, please. You are not in a..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. Soll, please. You are not in a position to judge us."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""I do, actually.""
entries.dialogueText: "I do, actually."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""It's the perfect retirement. An en..."
entries.dialogueText: "It's the perfect retirement. An entire island just for myself and my loved ones. And it's not even that expensive."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Imagine your very own miniature pa..."
entries.dialogueText: "Imagine your very own miniature paradise, with its topography custom-designed to suit your needs. Well, I don't need to imagine it -- I own one now."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""That reminds me of another former..."
entries.dialogueText: "That reminds me of another former president who lived on an island. Tarquin Soll."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Isn't that all a bit much? No need..."
entries.dialogueText: "Isn't that all a bit much? No need to be such a show-off."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Well... I find it disgusting.""
entries.dialogueText: "Well... I find it disgusting."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Good for you, I guess...""
entries.dialogueText: "Good for you, I guess..."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Oh, please.""
entries.dialogueText: "Oh, please."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Don't even make that comparison.""
entries.dialogueText: "Don't even make that comparison."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Oh, it is, thank you.""
entries.dialogueText: "Oh, it is, thank you."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Suit yourself.""
entries.dialogueText: "Suit yourself."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""And now Gasom is booming. We've al..."
entries.dialogueText: "And now Gasom is booming. We've all won."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""We've all benefited, just like I s..."
entries.dialogueText: "We've all benefited, just like I said. You, me, Gasom and Sordland."

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""How dare you, son. If we avoided w..."
entries.dialogueText: "How dare you, son. If we avoided war with Rumburg, it was by the skin of our teeth, not because you handed the Queen the key to our energy grid."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Thanks to President Rayne, Sordlan..."
entries.dialogueText: "Thanks to President Rayne, Sordland and Rumburg are set to become allies and business partners. Old enemies can still be future friends, Mr. Soll."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Ewald's upper lip curled, but he qu..."
entries.dialogueText: Ewald's upper lip curled, but he quickly turned it into a smile.

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""And now you're even boasting about..."
entries.dialogueText: "And now you're even boasting about how you climbed into bed with our enemies."

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""Don't speak like an idiot, Ewald...."
entries.dialogueText: "Don't speak like an idiot, Ewald. You made this deal long before diplomacy with Rumburg was in the cards."

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""Yet you did it anyway, knowing tha..."
entries.dialogueText: "Yet you did it anyway, knowing that war might be on the horizon. Just to line your pockets with Rumburgian crowns."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Soll is right about this. Rumburg..."
entries.dialogueText: "Soll is right about this. Rumburg should never have ended up with the largest share in Gasom."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Ewald, I must remind you that you..."
entries.dialogueText: "Ewald, I must remind you that you sold those shares before any diplomatic talks were being discussed. Don't use that as an excuse."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I don't begrudge Mr. Alphonso his..."
entries.dialogueText: "I don't begrudge Mr. Alphonso his decision. Especially since our relations with Rumburg have improved so much."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""He has the freedom to sell his per..."
entries.dialogueText: "He has the freedom to sell his personal assets to anyone he chooses. Including Rumburg."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""And Gasom is operating the same as..."
entries.dialogueText: "And Gasom is operating the same as ever. You don't even notice the difference in ownership."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Same as ever? It's a foreign-owned..."
entries.dialogueText: "Same as ever? It's a foreign-owned company and Rumburg has the biggest stake."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""That's good to hear. We can't risk..."
entries.dialogueText: "That's good to hear. We can't risk any deterioration of relations with Rumburg."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I must remind you that you sold th..."
entries.dialogueText: "I must remind you that you sold those shares before any diplomatic talks were being discussed. You handed our largest rival the keys to our energy grid."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""How can you casually bring this up..."
entries.dialogueText: "How can you casually bring this up? You sold off Gasom, just to line your pockets with Rumburgian crowns."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Mr. Rayne, please. You are not in..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. Rayne, please. You are not in a position to judge me."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""You didn't invest enough to help k..."
entries.dialogueText: "You didn't invest enough to help keep my company afloat, while opening the door to foreigners who were willing to do exactly that. What did you think would happen?"

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Rumburg and Rizia were never my fi..."
entries.dialogueText: "Rumburg and Rizia were never my first choices. But they came to Gasom's rescue when Sordland would not."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""I thought you'd be glad, Mr. Rayne..."
entries.dialogueText: "I thought you'd be glad, Mr. Rayne. If your goal is to avoid conflict with Rumburg, a stake in Gasom is one hell of a peace offering."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Gentlemen, please. Neither of you..."
entries.dialogueText: "Gentlemen, please. Neither of you can judge me."

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""I can't believe the two of you. Yo..."
entries.dialogueText: "I can't believe the two of you. You join my party and then undermine everything it stands for."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Exactly. And you are doing an extr..."
entries.dialogueText: "Exactly. And you are doing an extraordinary job on that front."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Mr. Soll, please. You are in no po..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. Soll, please. You are in no position to judge us."

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""No, but history will judge you. An..."
entries.dialogueText: "No, but history will judge you. And I suspect it will find you wanting."

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""You cannot trust a monarchy, gentl..."
entries.dialogueText: "You cannot trust a monarchy, gentlemen. Rizia and Rumburg will never be our friends."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""You should have been able to fix G..."
entries.dialogueText: "You should have been able to fix Gasom on your own, not go begging for investment."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Don't try to blame me for your own..."
entries.dialogueText: "Don't try to blame me for your own selfishness. I see now why Soll never trusted you."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""I did everything I could do on my..."
entries.dialogueText: "I did everything I could do on my own. But a company needs investors to truly thrive. Look at how it's been booming with Rumburg's involvement."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""We're putting stock in the old man..."
entries.dialogueText: "We're putting stock in the old man's opinion now?"

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""I've been starting to regret selli..."
entries.dialogueText: "I've been starting to regret selling my Gasom shares to Rumburg."

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""Relations? We are on the verge of..."
entries.dialogueText: "Relations? We are on the verge of war, Mr. Alphonso."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""I had no idea our relations would..."
entries.dialogueText: "I had no idea our relations would sink this low."

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""You handed our enemies the keys to..."
entries.dialogueText: "You handed our enemies the keys to our energy. And now you're acting as if you had no idea Rumburg posed a threat."

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""You are a traitor. It's that simpl..."
entries.dialogueText: "You are a traitor. It's that simple."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Ewald's upper lip curled."
entries.dialogueText: Ewald's upper lip curled.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Don't make me laugh. You always kn..."
entries.dialogueText: "Don't make me laugh. You always knew that Rumburg posed a threat. But you cared more about your precious free market than national security."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""This is my fault as much as it is..."
entries.dialogueText: "This is my fault as much as it is yours. I never should have removed the Energy Protection Act."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Sink this low? War is upon us, Ewa..."
entries.dialogueText: "Sink this low? War is upon us, Ewald. And you betrayed our nation by handing our enemies the keys to our energy."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Don't expect me to sympathize with..."
entries.dialogueText: "Don't expect me to sympathize with you. You sold off Gasom, just to line your pockets with Rumburgian crowns."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""I gave Sordland the first chance a..."
entries.dialogueText: "I gave Sordland the first chance at a large investment. I told you that completely removing the Energy Protection Act might compromise our interests."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Please, let's not go there.""
entries.dialogueText: "Please, let's not go there."

entries.dialogueText: "Blaming the USP for your own mistakes. That's an Ewald Alphonso move if I ever heard of one."

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""My footsteps? If it were up to me,..."
entries.dialogueText: "My footsteps? If it were up to me, Gasom would have been nationalized long ago to prevent exactly this from happening."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Excuse me, but that's bullshit and..."
entries.dialogueText: "Excuse me, but that's bullshit and you know it."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Leave me out of this. I've only ev..."
entries.dialogueText: "Leave me out of this. I've only ever tried to do what's right for Sordland."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""All you had to do was leave your i..."
entries.dialogueText: "All you had to do was leave your investment and the EPA untouched, Mr. Rayne. But that somehow proved too difficult for you."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The three of us glared at each othe..."
entries.dialogueText: The three of us glared at each other.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""It was never my intention to bankr..."
entries.dialogueText: "It was never my intention to bankrupt Gasom. I made my decisions with the company's interests at heart."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I was forced to revert the EPA to..."
entries.dialogueText: "I was forced to revert the EPA to 10 percent foreign ownership. The USP made me do it."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I'm sorry, Mr. Alphonso. But you g..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm sorry, Mr. Alphonso. But you got through it all unscathed, didn't you?"

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Of course I did. But Gasom is as m..."
entries.dialogueText: "Of course I did. But Gasom is as much a part of my legacy as my presidency. And now it's been tainted forever."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Do not blame your own shortcomings..."
entries.dialogueText: "Do not blame your own shortcomings on your party, Mr. President."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Excuse me, but that is bullshit an..."
entries.dialogueText: "Excuse me, but that is bullshit and you know it."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "We glared at each other."
entries.dialogueText: We glared at each other.

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""What are you talking about, Alphon..."
entries.dialogueText: "What are you talking about, Alphonso? I've read the reports. Your Gasom is doing fine without foreign investment propping it up."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""We are barely turning a profit. Al..."
entries.dialogueText: "We are barely turning a profit. All it would take is a bad few months for it all to come crashing down."

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""You cannot lay your own failures a..."
entries.dialogueText: "You cannot lay your own failures at the feet of the state, Alphonso."

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""Admit it. A man with your profit-f..."
entries.dialogueText: "Admit it. A man with your profit-focused mentality should have never been given the keys to such a vital sector, let alone the presidency."

entries.speaker: Tarquin Soll
entries.title: Tarquin Soll: ""Then that is your fault. Not the S..."
entries.dialogueText: "Then that is your fault. Not the Sordish state's."
